blocks.text: Ranch Park Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Ranch Park is the house pocket around Spuraway Avenue and the north side of Mariner Way in central Coquitlam, with Mundy Park's forest as its south edge; the City publishes no boundary for this board sub-area name, so treat street names, not a map line, as the check.
The pocket's addressed anchor is Ranch Park Elementary at 2701 Spuraway Avenue, the School District No. 43 (Coquitlam) school inside the street pattern.
The City's trail guide maps Spuraway Avenue and Mariner Way along Mundy Park's north side, with the park's parking lot and community path reached from those streets.

blocks.text: Ranch Park Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The City tells owners to contact Development Services before designing a small-scale project if there is a creek on or next to the lot, a steep slope on or next to it, or the house was built before 1945 — a live question for lots backing onto the Mundy Park and Riverview Forest green space.

Plan status needs a current check: the whole city now sits under the Interim Official Community Plan (OCP), Bylaw No. 5511, 2026, adopted April 27, 2026, which replaced Citywide OCP Bylaw No. 3479, 2001.

blocks.text: Ranch Park Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Dogs must be on leash at all times on the Mundy Park Community Path, and the trail guide directs dog owners to the park's separate off-leash rules — a daily-life detail for houses whose yards open toward the park.

The Mundy Park Community Path can be completed on foot within an hour and is a paved multi-use trail suitable for a variety of recreational pursuits, so the park edge carries steady walker and cyclist traffic past the Spuraway Avenue side.

Mundy Park holds an outdoor pool, listed as Spani Pool on the City's trail guide map, with playground, washrooms and parking inside the park — seasonal recreation on this pocket's doorstep, not a year-round facility.
Riverview Forest, beside Mundy Park, is a dedicated urban forest with trails for walking and jogging in a forested natural setting, extending the green edge east of the Ranch Park streets.
Route 152, Coquitlam Central Station to Lougheed Station, runs the length of Mariner Way at the pocket's west and south sides via Dewdney Trunk Road, with some trips via Chilko Drive.
Route 153, Coquitlam Central Station to Braid Station, runs Mariner Way via Como Lake Avenue, Laurentian Crescent, Austin Avenue and Poirier Street.

blocks.text: Ranch Park Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check creek status on any lot draining toward Mundy Park: the City classifies its creeks for environmental value and monitors flow, level and water quality on various creeks, and a park-edge lot still needs its own mapping check before purchase.

Ranch Park home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

32 houses sold in Ranch Park with a median price of $1,485,000 (the middle half sold between $1,384,625 and $1,796,000), taking a median of 24 days to sell at 95.6% of the last list price; 9% sold above list. They had a median $579 per square foot, a median year built of 1973 and a median lot of 8,911 square feet.

Its Mundy Park Community Path is a 5.5-kilometre paved multi-use trail encircling the park, and shorter interior trails loop around Mundy Lake and lead to viewing benches at Lost Lake.

Route 153 also runs Mariner Way, linking Coquitlam Central Station with Braid Station in New Westminster via Como Lake Avenue.
